title: The Broken Ember Again
premise: Casper Hartwell, a scribe indentured to the Ledger Guild of Vharen, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are fragments of a country called Ossuary that was erased from memory two centuries ago — and that the child, Ember, is its last living citizen. The ledgers Casper keeps are actually binding contracts holding what remains of Ossuary in stasis, and the dragon-fire that sustains it is dying. To free Ember and herself from debt, Casper must reconstruct the true ledger, find the door out of a country that no longer exists, and choose whether to restore Ossuary at the cost of her own remembered life. In the end she burns her own name from the guild's books, walks Ember through the door into the world, and lets the last ember gutter out — carrying only memory forward.
about_author: August Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the papers of defunct trading companies before turning to fiction. They write about bureaucracy as magic and magic as debt, and live somewhere with too many locked drawers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A day in the Ledger Guild: Casper tallies impossible inventory — bottled thunder, a widow's second shadow — while calculating her unpayable debt. Emotional beat: weary competence masking quiet despair; establishes the cost of every mistake in a world where bookkeeping is binding.

chapters.title: A Knock in Old Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At closing bell, a mud-streaked girl arrives speaking a language no living scholar knows — yet Casper's hand translates it on the page before her mind catches up. The guild masters seal the doors. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as Casper realizes her own ink is complicit.

chapters.title: What the Guild Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Interrogated by Master Quillon, Casper learns the girl is 'inventory' — an asset logged two hundred years ago under a contract still accruing interest. Casper is assigned as her custodian, a punishment disguised as trust. Beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Ember
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the scriptorium attic, Casper names the girl Ember and coaxes fragments of her story: a country called Ossuary, a fire that never went out, adults who forgot her name one by one. Beat: tenderness breaking through Casper's transactional worldview.

chapters.title: The Forgetting of Ossuary
chapters.summary: POV Ember. Through Ember's eyes we see Ossuary whole: dragon-fire lamps, doors that open onto yesterday, a people who traded memories like coin. Then the erasure begins mid-scene, words dissolving off her tongue. Beat: grief rendered as sensory loss.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper finds her own family name in the oldest volume — her grandmother sold something to the guild, and Casper's debt is inherited interest on it. She confronts Quillon and learns the ledgers don't record trade; they enforce forgetting. Beat: betrayal and fury.

chapters.title: The Fire Under the Floor
chapters.summary: POV Ember. Ember senses the dragon-fire beneath the guildhall guttering and leads Casper down through sealed sub-levels to a vast furnace room where a sleeping flame breathes like a lung. Beat: awe and dread; the stakes become physical and time-bound.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The guild moves to liquidate Ember — converting her remaining memories into sellable assets. Casper falsifies an entry to buy time, committing her first true crime against the books. Beat: the thrill and terror of becoming a forger.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Drowned
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Following a marginal note in her grandmother's hand, Casper seeks a disgraced guild cartographer living drunk above a fishmonger's, who once mapped the borders of Ossuary before they were unwritten. Beat: wary alliance; the past has allies.

chapters.title: Borders That Unwrite
chapters.summary: POV Ember. Ember teaches Casper the old tongue's grammar of place — how Ossuary's doors were anchored in spoken names. As they practice, Casper's own memories begin flickering: the guild notices her treason. Beat: intimacy deepening alongside danger.

chapters.title: Quillon's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Cornered, Quillon reveals he was born in Ossuary and bought his survival by helping write the erasure; his cruelty is guilt wearing armor. He warns them the fire has days left. Beat: moral complexity — the villain as fellow prisoner.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Sold
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the deep archive, Casper uncovers her grandmother's original contract: she sold the location of Ossuary's last door to save her daughter — Casper's mother — from being forgotten. Beat: inheritance reframed; Casper's debt is love, compounded.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: POV Ember. The guild auctions Ossuary's residual assets publicly. Ember watches strangers bid on her mother's lullaby, her city's rain. Casper bids everything she doesn't have to win back one small vial of memory. Beat: public humiliation, private defiance.

chapters.title: Run
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Exposed as a forger, Casper flees with Ember through the guildhall's shifting corridors as the building itself — a ledger made stone — tries to balance their escape against its books. Beat: pure momentum; the architecture turns hostile.

chapters.title: The Country That Remembers Us
chapters.summary: POV Ember. Hiding in the drowned cartographer's maps, Ember pulls Casper into a memory-vision of Ossuary at its height, showing her the door out stands inside the guild's founding vault. Beat: belonging — Casper feels, briefly, like a citizen of somewhere.

chapters.title: Allies of the Unwritten
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The cartographer, Quillon, and other descendants of the erased converge; each carries a fragment — a word, a street name, a recipe — that can rebuild the true ledger. Beat: hope assembled from scraps; community as counter-magic.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the True Book
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A night of feverish collaboration: the fragments are entered into a new ledger written in Ember's tongue, which the guild's bindings cannot parse. The fire below gutters to a thread. Beat: exhausted determination racing extinction.

chapters.title: The Founding Vault
chapters.summary: POV Ember. The company breaches the vault and finds the door out of Ossuary — sealed behind the guild's first contract, signed in ash. Opening it requires a name freely given to be struck from all records. Beat: the price becomes clear and personal.

chapters.title: Strike My Name
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax begins: guild enforcers arrive; Quillon holds the line at terrible cost. Casper offers her own name — her inheritance, her identity, her debt — to the ash. Beat: sacrifice chosen not from heroism but from finally understanding what matters.

chapters.title: The Last Guttering
chapters.summary: POV Ember. The dragon-fire dies as the door opens; Ossuary exhales its final two centuries in a single warm wind. Ember must choose: step through alone into a world that will forget her, or stay and vanish with her country. Beat: heartbreak at the threshold.

chapters.title: Through the Door Out
chapters.summary: POV Casper, now nameless. Casper takes Ember's hand and crosses; without a name, the world cannot re-file her, and the two walk out of the guild's jurisdiction entirely. Behind them, the guildhall's ledgers blank themselves page by page. Beat: liberation as erasure.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ember (coda). Weeks later, in a coastal town, a woman with no past and a girl with an ancient one open a shop that mends broken memories for pay-what-you-can. On the first page of a fresh notebook, Ember writes both their names. Beat: belonging rebuilt, chosen this time.
